Messages.Author: Rob LeGood
Messages.Body:
This came up last night whilst playing..

Can a minion block a directed action against him/her?
i.e. VampA attempts to Bum's Rush VampB. VampB wishes to block this
action for the sole purpose of preventing VampA from getting the
optional press.

Is this legal?

rob.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
Rob LeGood <rfle...@ix.netcom.com> writes:

> Can a minion block a directed action against him/her?

The answer you're looking for is "yes, it can".

To be technical, the answer is "unknown and not relevant". Directed
actions are derected against a Methuseleh, not a vampire. Even if the
action would affect one of the Meth's vampires, it's still directed at the
Meth, not the vampire.

> i.e. VampA attempts to Bum's Rush VampB. VampB wishes to block this
>action for the sole purpose of preventing VampA from getting the
>optional press.

> Is this legal?

Yes, and common as well.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
curt...@aol.com (CurtAdams) writes:

>Rob LeGood <rfle...@ix.netcom.com> writes:

>> Can a minion block a directed action against him/her?

>The answer you're looking for is "yes, it can".

Correct.

>To be technical, the answer is "unknown and not relevant". Directed
>actions are derected against a Methuseleh, not a vampire. Even if the
>action would affect one of the Meth's vampires, it's still directed at the
>Meth, not the vampire.

Not so. It *is* directed at the vampire. As a directed action, it
can be blocked only by the controller of the target. The distinction
is relevant to several Sabbat cards:

Blessing of Chaos Action Dementation 1 blood
This is a +1 stealth action.
Normal: Put this card on the acting vampire. If the vampire with this
card attempts to block another vampire, that vampire cannot play
action modifiers requiring Dementation, Dominate, Presence, or
Chimerstry. Vampires opposing this vampire in combat cannot play
cards that require those Disciplines.
Superior: As above, and actions requiring those Disciplines cannot be
directed at this vampire.

Communal Haven: Temple Master Sabbat 1 pool
Master: location. Each Sabbat vampire you control gets +1 intercept
when attempting to block (D) actions directed against other Sabbat
vampires you control. A player may have only one Communal Haven in
play.

Consecration Rites Action
Requires a ready Priscus, Cardinal, or Archbishop.
This is a +1 stealth action.
Put this card on a location you control. You may burn this card to cause
an action directed at the location to fail.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu (L. Scott Johnson) writes:

>curt...@aol.com (CurtAdams) writes:

>>To be technical, the answer is "unknown and not relevant". Directed
>>actions are derected against a Methuseleh, not a vampire. Even if the
>>action would affect one of the Meth's vampires, it's still directed at
the
>>Meth, not the vampire.

>Not so. It *is* directed at the vampire. As a directed action, it
>can be blocked only by the controller of the target.

Directed actions are directed against Methuselehs. From the original
rulebook, 13.3.1:

"Non-directed actions are actions that are not directed against a
*Methuseleh*" (emphasis mine).

There is a casual meaning of "directed", meaning "affecting", and in that
sense Bum's Rush is indeed "directed" at a vampire. But in the technical
word "directed" in game terms refers to who is allowed to block. For the
casual use of "directed" you would need another term like "targeting".

>Communal Haven: Temple Master Sabbat 1 pool
> Master: location. Each Sabbat vampire you control gets +1 intercept
> when attempting to block (D) actions directed against other Sabbat
> vampires you control. A player may have only one Communal Haven in
> play.

So WotC doesn't know its own terminology and is confusing the casual and
game meanings of "directed". So what's new? They can't get their
templates straight either.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
curt...@aol.com (CurtAdams) writes:
>sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu (L. Scott Johnson) writes:
>>curt...@aol.com (CurtAdams) writes:
>>>To be technical, the answer is "unknown and not relevant". Directed
>>>actions are derected against a Methuseleh, not a vampire. Even if the
>>>action would affect one of the Meth's vampires, it's still directed at
>the
>>>Meth, not the vampire.

>>Not so. It *is* directed at the vampire. As a directed action, it
>>can be blocked only by the controller of the target.

>Directed actions are directed against Methuselehs. From the original
>rulebook, 13.3.1:

>"Non-directed actions are actions that are not directed against a
>*Methuseleh*" (emphasis mine).

An action directed at a Methuselah's minion is also directed at that
Methuselah, yes. But it is still directed at the minion as well.

In the VtES rules, this overlap is more obvious. But it still exists
in Jyhad. The case can be made (and you make it very well) that the
overlap didn't exist in Jyhad, but there is no proof for either side
of the argument. And, since the VtES rules don't conflict with the
Jyhad rules on this matter, I'd suggest simply assuming that it works
the same way in Jyhad.

>So WotC doesn't know its own terminology and is confusing the casual and
>game meanings of "directed". So what's new? They can't get their
>templates straight either.

An action is either Directed or not. Directed actions are always:

(The following terms are used interchangeably in the VtES rulebook to
describe/define a directed action)
directed at
directed against
targeted at
directly affect

a Methuselah or a card that a Methuselah controls

(Actually, the rulebook only notes minions that a Methuselah controls,
ignoring the fact that some directed action target other cards - like
Arson, Cryptic Mission (vs. Retainers), inferior Shepherd's Innocence, etc.)

Messages.Author: Bishop Vesey's Grammar
Messages.Body:
Okay, some of the things are only directed at things another Methuselah
controls (these are stated specifically on the cards). However, what
happens if the thing does not state it eg. Darius Styx.

He specifically states that it can be directed at *any* Methuselah.

I have seen the official line on this ie it can't.

However, I don't like the way it has been resolved - you can't because
(D) actions can't be directed at yourself unless the card specifically
over-rules this.

Darius' wording *does* over-rule this.

I'm not complaining about the ruling - Ravnos weapon decks would go wild
- but I am complaining about how it's been fixed. Surely just an errata
- Direct the action at any other Met - would do, not saying the card
doesn't say that when it quite clearly does.

---

James Coupe.
